speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash on both upper extremities; can you tell me when you first noticed it and if the itching is constant or intermittent?

To better understand the cause, have you noticed any new medications, soaps, or environmental exposures recently?

Finally, does the rash spread to other areas of your body, or is it strictly limited to your arms?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pityriasis Rosea (likely early presentation given 5-month duration is atypical for classic course, consider secondary syphilis or chronic eczema). REQUEST TEST: RPR, TPHA. REQUEST IMAGES: Rash_Upper_Extremities
